objective: Move the performance evidence beyond one startup benchmark: record the resolved commit and environment with every report, report P99 and a measured failure rate with explicit units, add budgets for event-log size, per-run disk growth, concurrent runs, API latency and API/telemetry failure rate, bound the readiness probe by its caller's deadline and name the timeout cause, wire the absolute budgets into a scheduled workflow that needs no Docker or committed baseline, and keep simulation and hardware evidence unmerged.
decision_supported: Can a reviewer see from a report alone which commit and environment produced it, compare P50/P95/P99 latency and a counted failure rate with units, and fail a build on an event-log, disk-growth, concurrency, API-latency or failure-rate budget breach rather than only on startup time?
acceptance: every performance report records the resolved git revision alongside platform, Python and machine, and comparability stays keyed on the environment fields plus cache mode rather than on the commit
a commit that is not a 7-40 character lowercase hex object name is refused instead of being recorded
stage telemetry reports P50, P95, P99 and max, each with an explicit unit, so a bare number cannot be compared as if it were milliseconds

failures are counted from the records themselves via an ERROR/CRITICAL level or a declared failure event, one record counts at most once even when it carries both signals, and a quiet run is not reported as failing
budgets exist and are enforced for event-log bytes, per-run disk growth, concurrent runs, API P50/P95/P99 latency and API failure rate, alongside the existing startup, CPU and memory budgets

the resource producer measures the event-log bytes, per-run growth, concurrent runs and read-only API latency and failure rate it now reports, tolerating a single failed probe as measurement rather than aborting the run
the telemetry failure rate is checked against the counts it claims, and a rate that contradicts its own numerator and denominator is refused
the readiness probe is bounded by the caller's deadline rather than a fixed sleep, and an exhausted budget raises an error naming the attempt count and the last observed cause
a report missing the event-log or API object is refused rather than defaulting those budgets to zero

a budget-only mode checks absolute budgets without a committed baseline, records every metric whose report was not supplied under not_evaluated, reports INCOMPLETE rather than PASS for a partial run, and exits non-zero so a scheduled job can gate on it

a scheduled workflow runs the scripts-only policy with pinned actions and read-only permissions, uploads the budget report, and states in its summary that target-hardware and physical measurements remain NOT_EXECUTED

simulation and hardware metrics cannot be combined without provenance: hardware telemetry still requires a hash-verified operator evidence manifest, and the software gate accepts simulation telemetry only
evidence: Task Packet schema validation output with exit code
targeted pytest output listing the collected Issue #79 test names, pass counts and exit codes
make performance-budget-check output showing the parsed revision, the three checked metrics, the exit code, and the written report
a real analyze_telemetry run over 30 scripted iterations showing p99_ms, the unit label and a counted failure rate for every stage
a budget-only run over a single supplied report showing status INCOMPLETE with the unsupplied metrics listed under not_evaluated and exit code 2
a budget-only run over the scripts-only policy showing status PASS and exit code 0
mutation probe 1 output: with failure classification disabled, the failure-counting tests fail
mutation probe 2 output: with p99 replaced by p50, the p99 test fails
mutation probe 3 output: with a fixed sleep in the readiness probe, the bounded-readiness test fails
mutation probe 4 output: with commit format validation relaxed, the bogus-commit cases fail
mutation probe 5 output: with missing event_log and api objects defaulted to zero, the missing-evidence test fails
each mutation probe restored byte-identically, confirmed with diff -q against the pre-probe snapshot
ruff check, ruff format --check, the full pytest run, make contract, make scenario-check, make golden-check, make context-check and make docs output with exit codes
final git diff --check and git diff --name-only output proving every changed path is allowed
stop_conditions: Meeting the acceptance requires changing a producer of robot or runtime telemetry, an interface schema, a service under services/, or a path owned by another module.
The gate claims a relative regression without a baseline, or a hardware measurement without attested physical evidence.
A missing report or a metric with no data is reported as PASS instead of INCOMPLETE or FAIL.
A budget threshold is applied to a metric whose unit is not recorded.
The scheduled workflow requires Docker, a second host or a committed machine-specific baseline.
data_classification: internal; tests and reports use synthetic stage names, synthetic durations, synthetic container names and synthetic run identifiers, and read no real robot, camera, credential or operator data
model_policy: no model call; percentile computation, failure counting, budget comparison and readiness probing are deterministic
risks_and_fallbacks: A budget that only covers startup time cannot catch a regression in the runtime it is meant to protect. Event-log size, per-run disk growth, concurrency, API latency and failure rate are now budgeted too, each from a measured producer rather than a placeholder.

A quiet pipeline is not a passing one. Failures are counted from the records themselves and a count that contradicts its own denominator is refused, so a dropped producer cannot lower the measured rate.

A relative threshold with no baseline is unfalsifiable. Budget-only mode checks absolute limits, marks unsupplied reports as not_evaluated, reports INCOMPLETE, and exits non-zero, so a partial scheduled run cannot read as a green one.

A fixed sleep in a readiness probe both overshoots a short deadline and hides its own cause. The probe now caps each wait by the time actually remaining and names the attempt count and last observed cause on timeout.

Adding a scheduled workflow touches CI configuration, which AGENTS.md routes to integration review. The workflow is additive, uses pinned actions, requests contents: read only, and gates on budgets that are enforced locally by the same command; the change is called out for reviewer attention.

Recording the commit in the environment block would have made every report incomparable across commits. The revision is stored as a separate top-level field, and comparability remains keyed on platform, Python, machine and cache mode.

A hosted CI runner is a different host class from the development machine. The scheduled policy declares only the metrics that host can produce and keeps clear headroom, while target hardware, ROS/Gazebo and physical measurements stay NOT_EXECUTED.
